Each cut is a real edit that jumps to a completely different framing — no dissolve, no fade, no morph, no continuous camera move across the cut; the image visibly snaps from one shot to the next. Real-time motion. No subtitles, no music.

OPTICS
LENS LOCK SHOT 1 = 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens, camera ~2 m back, the small cabin corner and both sconces readable.
LENS LOCK SHOT 2 = 18° diagonal field of view, tight detail lens, camera very close on one lamp; the glowing lamp fills the frame, shallow focus, soft background falloff.
LENS LOCK SHOT 3 = 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens, camera ~1.5–2 m from the subject, natural human-eye perspective, medium shot cropped at the waist.
No lens drift within any shot.

CAMERA
All shots use a static locked composition — no pan, tilt, dolly, or zoom; each frame holds its position. Handheld texture only: subtle operator breath and faint pulse, human micro-correction, never digital jitter or gimbal glide. Shots 1 and 2 are held nearly still. In Shot 3, on each floor impact the handheld frame absorbs a small sympathetic jolt, grounded and physical.

FIRST FRAME AND SHOT BLOCKING
SHOT 1 (0.0–1.5s): empty cabin, no person. A held wide of the corner and its two warm sconces, establishing the space. Static.
1.5s HARD CUT.
SHOT 2 (1.5–2.5s): extreme close-up of one scalloped frosted-glass "cloud" wall sconce only, filling the frame, glowing warm and soft. No person, no camera move. Static insert.
2.5s HARD CUT.
SHOT 3 (2.5–8.0s): the first frame after the cut already contains the man — no delayed reveal. He stands in the corner of the cabin, back fully to camera, occupying the left vertical third, framed waist-up: bald head around x=30%, y=20%; shoulders and jacketed back spanning x=14–46%; the bottom edge crops at his waist near y=96%. His head is bowed downward, looking at the floor directly in front of his feet — his target is on the ground, not the wall. His knee, feet, and the floor stay below the bottom frame edge and are never seen; all effort reads through a large vertical travel of the upper body.

ACTION TIMING
SHOT 1 (0.0–1.5s): static empty cabin, held.
SHOT 2 (1.5–2.5s): static extreme close-up of the sconce, held.
SHOT 3 (2.5–8.0s): the man hammers his right boot straight down into the floor with maximum force, over and over, as if crushing something underfoot. Because the frame is cropped at the waist, his knee, foot and the floor are out of frame — all of this violence reads through a big vertical travel of the visible upper body.
Each strike is one committed blow with a clear beat between blows (~1.2–1.5s per cycle):
(1) WIND-UP — he rears up tall: the whole torso and shoulders rise high as the hidden knee lifts up hard, spine lengthening, body coiling with furious tension, head still aimed down at the target on the floor.
(2) SLAM — he throws his entire body weight explosively straight down; torso and shoulders drop fast and low as the boot drives vertically into the floor, then a hard recoil snaps back up through the spine and the jacket creases and jolts.
About 4 heavy, escalating strikes across the shot — each a single powerful vertical stomp with a full wind-up, never rapid little steps or shuffling. Hollywood-level rage: he pours all his anger and his full body weight into every downward blow.

PHYSICS
Real body mass and gravity. The strike vector is strictly vertical — straight down into the floor beneath him; the boot never travels forward and never contacts, kicks, or touches the walls or the corner. Full weight transfers into each downward strike; hard boot-on-solid-floor contact with no give. The floor is extremely hard and does not crack, dent, deform, or break — every impact rebounds sharply back up through ankle, knee, hips, and spine. Inertia and follow-through are visible in the shoulders and in the swinging weight of the jacket. Grounded, heavy, repeated impacts; no floating, no rubbery motion.

LIGHTING
The only light is the cabin's own warm practical sconces — two scalloped frosted-glass wall lights glowing weak, soft, and diffuse. The deep reddish-brown padded walls swallow most of the light, keeping the cabin low-key, warm, and moody. In Shot 3, soft warm ambient spill grazes the man's back and bald head; everything else falls into soft-edged warm shadow. Light comes only from these practical sconces — no added film lighting, no key light, no white light, no hard rim, no direct beam on him. Soft natural diffuse practical light only.

AUDIO
No dialogue, no music. Shots 1 and 2: quiet, near-silent cabin tone. From Shot 3: the dull, heavy thud of a boot striking a solid, unyielding floor — flat impacts with no cracking or breaking sound, because the floor never gives — plus the man's strained, furious breathing and low grunts of exertion, inside the tight, reverberant cabin.

POSITIVE LOCKS
- Three shots joined by two instant hard cuts at 1.5s and 2.5s; the image visibly jumps at each cut and is never a continuous animation of a single frame.
- Every strike goes strictly straight DOWN into the floor; the boot never hits, kicks, or touches the walls or the corner — he is stomping the ground, not the wall.
- He never marches, shuffles, or steps in place; each blow is one big vertical wind-up (torso rising high, knee lifted) followed by one explosive slam straight down, with a beat between blows.
- The upper body shows a large vertical travel — a high rise on the wind-up and a hard drop on impact — not a small bob or fidget.
- Only <<<image_2>>> appears, and only in Shot 3; no other person at any point.
- <<<image_2>>> stays in the left third, back to camera, framed at the waist; his legs, feet, and the floor are never visible.
- The floor never breaks, cracks, or deforms under the strikes.
- Light comes only from the cabin's own warm practical sconces — soft, weak, diffuse; no added, white, or direct light on him.

His partner has been waiting in an armchair, snacking, and needles him. Five-shot dialogue scene, 35mm analog sci-fi film look. Every performance beat is played with Hollywood-caliber emotional precision and nuanced micro-expression.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
@ROOM — first reference image: round retro-futuristic control room; domed ceiling, ring of warm marquee bulbs, curved walls of vintage instrument panels and glowing CRT screens, dark red carpet, angular metal water tank with churning blue-lit water on screen-left, plush red armchair on screen-right facing the tank, thick cables snaking across the carpet and draping over the tank rim. Reference controls room geometry, materials, furniture placement and atmosphere only; its camera angle is not inherited.
@ADIL — second reference image: man in his late twenties, shoulder-length wet dark curly hair, thin mustache and small chin beard, wearing a dark-green neural-interface wetsuit with rust-orange collar and side panels, white electrode pads with thin pale wires stuck to his chest, arms, temples and forehead. 100% matches the reference.
@CHANG — third reference image: bald East-Asian man around thirty, bleached eyebrows, scar across his left eyebrow, pale-blue left eye, dragon tattoo running down the right side of his skull and neck, rust-orange suede bomber jacket with golden Monkey King embroidery over a white tee, silver chain. 100% matches the reference.
@CHIPS — fourth reference image: metallic-green foil snack bag with an orange-and-black biohazard emblem and a transparent window showing spiral purple-and-orange chips; the chips themselves are tight spiral curls, purple and orange. 100% matches the reference.

LOCATION MAP
Inside @ROOM the water tank and the red armchair face each other about 4 meters apart across the red carpet; cables run between them. The angular metal tank is long enough for a man to lie fully stretched out inside it. It has a near front corner — the corner of its rim pointing into the middle of the room toward the armchair, the closest point of the tank to the armchair, where thick cables drape over the rim down to the carpet. A small folded dark-grey towel lies on that near front corner of the rim from the very first frame of the scene and stays in exactly that position until it is grabbed in shot 5. Dialogue axis for shots 4 and 5: @ADIL in the tank looks screen-right toward @CHANG; @CHANG in the armchair looks screen-left toward @ADIL; the camera does not cross this axis in those shots.

FORMAT MODE
CONTROLLED MULTI-SHOT SEQUENCE, 15.0s total, five shots, hard cuts at 2.0s, 5.5s, 9.0s and 12.0s.

SHOT 1 — 0.0s-2.0s — static, from behind the armchair, identity withheld, chip pulled from the bag
First frame: camera locked on a tripod at seated-head height directly behind the red plush armchair; the chair's tall red backrest fills the right foreground from x 55-95% in soft focus, completely hiding whoever sits in it — only a man's forearm resting on the armrest is visible, hand holding the open green @CHIPS bag around x 58-72%, y 55-72%. Across the room in the deep background the metal tank sits around x 8-45%, its water glowing faint blue, the folded dark-grey towel lying on the near front corner of its rim; nobody is visible in the tank or anywhere else in the room. 0.4s-1.8s: the visible hand dips into the bag and pulls out ONE spiral chip — a tight purple-and-orange spiral curl exactly as in the @CHIPS reference — and holds it up between thumb and forefinger; this is the same chip he will eat later. The camera does not move at all — fully static frame; the seated figure's face and head are never revealed. Camera: 47° FOV.

SHOT 2 — 2.0s-5.5s — overhead MEDIUM shot, waist-up from directly above: violent terror wake-up
First frame: camera directly overhead, about 1.2 meters above the water surface, framing @ADIL from the waist up — a MEDIUM top-down shot, not a wide of the whole tank. @ADIL lies flat on his back along the length of the tank, fully submerged just under the surface: body stretched out straight and fully contained inside the tank basin, spine straight, shoulders level, arms relaxed along his sides, head resting centered — a natural, anatomically correct lying pose that fits the tank's shape; eyes closed, wired electrodes on his temples, dark curls floating. 2.2s-2.6s: his eyes SNAP open in a split second — instantly wide with raw terror, brows shooting up, pupils tiny — his mouth clamped firmly shut, breath held, absolutely no inhaling underwater, a violent full-body flinch. 2.6s-3.6s: he explodes upward out of the water — a fast, panicked, powerful burst, palms planting on the tank floor and rim as his torso rockets upright with one heavy splash — and ONLY once his face is fully clear of the water does he take his first huge ragged gasp of air. The rise is anatomically natural: torso hinging up from the hips, arms pushing, no distorted limbs. He stays inside the tank. 3.6s-5.5s: he sits bolt upright, chest heaving, terror still on his face, water streaming off him.

SHOT 3 — 5.5s-9.0s — strict profile on @ADIL: fear, stomach check, relief, turn to camera
First frame: camera perpendicular to the tank at chest height, 1.5 meters away, 47° FOV; @ADIL framed waist-up in strict profile, nose pointing screen-left, sitting upright in the tank, dripping, breathing fast, face still gripped by fear, the blue glow of the tank water softly lighting his face from below. 5.7s-7.0s: THE STOMACH CHECK — still scared, he looks down sharply and presses both palms flat against his stomach, one firm deliberate press through the wetsuit, checking that his belly is intact and nothing is protruding; he holds the press, eyes fixed on his own belly. 7.0s-7.9s: relief floods his face — the fear visibly drains away, one long slow exhale, shoulders dropping. 7.9s-9.0s: calmed, he turns to his right, head and shoulders rotating out of profile until he faces directly into the camera lens, eyes locked into the lens, wet and drained.

SHOT 4 — 9.0s-12.0s — 3/4 medium on @CHANG in the armchair
First frame: @CHANG framed waist-up in 3/4 view at x 35-70%, sitting relaxed and sunk into the red plush armchair, body angled screen-left toward the tank, eyes locked screen-left on @ADIL, amused smirk; the open @CHIPS bag in his left hand, the spiral purple-orange chip he pulled out in shot 1 still in his right fingers. 9.3s-10.5s: he says, dry and mocking: "So. Death by bird." 10.7s-11.2s: he pops the chip into his mouth. 11.2s-12.0s: he crunches it loudly, smirking, eyebrows raised, eyes never leaving @ADIL screen-left. Camera: locked-off, 1.5 meters away, 47° FOV.

SHOT 5 — 12.0s-15.0s — 3/4 medium on @ADIL, mirrored reverse of shot 4, towel grab
First frame: exact mirrored reverse angle of shot 4 across the dialogue axis: @ADIL framed chest-up in 3/4 view at x 30-65%, sitting in the tank, body and eyes toward screen-right at @CHANG, wet curls dripping, electrode pads on his temples, the blue water glow softly lighting his face from below; the folded dark-grey towel visible on the near front corner of the tank rim at the lower edge of frame, in the same position it held in shot 1. 12.2s-13.2s: confident and assertive, chin up, certain he has the winning argument, he fires back "It was the glass" — and while saying it he reaches down and grabs the towel off the rim corner in one self-assured motion. 13.4s-14.2s: the confidence cracks — hearing his own words he deflates and finishes much quieter, unsure: "...actually..." — and covers the embarrassment by starting to towel his wet hair, rubbing the towel over his curls, eyes sliding away from @CHANG. 14.2s-15.0s: he keeps drying his hair, sheepish, shoulders shrunk. Camera: locked-off, 1.5 meters away, 47° FOV.

OPTICS
35mm anamorphic analog film look, fine grain, soft halation on the dimmed bulbs and CRT screens, gentle focus breathing. 47° FOV on all shots; the overhead shot is a tighter medium framing from directly above, not a wide.

LIGHTING
No cinematic lighting sources of any kind: no key light, no rim light, no backlight, no hair light, no spotlights, no dramatic beams. The room is dim, noticeably darker than a standard interior, lit only by its own practicals — sparse warm panel lamps and the marquee bulb ring dimmed to a faint amber glow, CRT screens reduced to gentle colored washes — all heavily diffused. Faces are lit exclusively by this soft, wrapped, diffused ambient light: big-source softness, gradual falloff, deep soft shadows, no hard edges, no specular hotspots. In every shot where @ADIL is in the tank, the churning water casts a soft diffused blue underlight up onto his face from below, exactly as in the reference — gentle, wide and shadowless, mixing with the warm ambient. Faces stay readable through this soft ambient and the water glow alone.

PHYSICS
@ADIL's body always obeys real human anatomy: when lying he fits the tank naturally, limbs straight and proportioned; when rising, the movement is a real push — palms braced, torso hinging up — with no bent, broken or misplaced limbs. Water carries real mass: the explosive burst throws one heavy splash, sheets and drips keep running off his hair, mustache and electrode wires for seconds afterwards; the surface keeps sloshing against the tank walls after he sits up. The wet suit glistens softly. The towel lifts with real cloth weight and darkens where it touches wet hair and skin. The foil chip bag crinkles as the hand digs in; the chip crunches loudly between teeth.

AUDIO
Ambient: low analog equipment hum, faint CRT whine, water slosh; no music. Shot 1: soft foil crinkle as the chip is pulled out; no voices. Shot 2: muffled underwater near-silence, breath held, no bubbles — the first huge ragged gasp sounds only after his face breaks the surface, never before. Shot 3: fast frightened breathing settling into one long exhale; no words. Shot 4: @CHANG's line "So. Death by bird." in a dry, teasing baritone, followed by a loud chip crunch. Shot 5: @ADIL's "It was the glass" delivered confident and firm, then "...actually..." quiet, deflating, embarrassed, half-muffled as he towels his hair. Two distinct male voices. No other voices; lips move only during scripted lines.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Exactly two people exist in the scene: @ADIL inside the tank and @CHANG in the armchair. In shot 1 the seated figure stays anonymous, the camera stays fully static, and the hand pulls exactly one purple-and-orange spiral chip from the bag — the same chip eaten in shot 4. The dark-grey towel lies on the near front corner of the tank rim from the first frame of shot 1 and stays in that exact position until @ADIL grabs it in shot 5. @ADIL's body stays anatomically correct at all times — lying straight inside the tank, rising with a natural push, no broken or distorted poses — and he stays inside the tank for the entire scene. His first breath happens only above the water surface, never underwater. The stomach check in shot 3 happens exactly once and must be clearly visible: fear → both palms pressed to the stomach → relief. @CHANG simply puts the chip in his mouth and crunches — nothing more elaborate. Both faces 100% match their references whenever visible. Hard cuts exactly at 2.0s, 5.5s, 9.0s and 12.0s. Every emotional beat — sudden terror, relief, smugness, confidence cracking into embarrassment — is acted with Hollywood-caliber precision under purely soft diffused light.
